ABOUT THE AUTHOR: Born in Bowraville NSW, Allen Gillon qualified as a Teacher for the NSW Department Of Education in 1964, spending almost 25 years as a Primary Teacher. During that time Mr Gillon completed additional courses in musical arrangement at Sydney Conservatorium Of Music. He has written and had published a number of classroom texts, currently in use in Australian Schools. His musical training and experience resulted in his being granted many play and drama assignments, including a huge production of “Oliver” in the Penrith Department Region in 1977, co-ordinating 3 Primary schools, a 250 piece choir and a 13 member orchestra. Mr Gillon’s love of writing and school performances led him to write and produce many plays. Public acceptance and the success of these plays led to the production of this publication.

Aschool Choir can be added off-stage to enhance the songs sung by the cast. Others can be animals of the forest. This is a short play that can include many students in the cast.

The Play
ACT 1 Scene 1 Inside view of a lavish state room with throne. The Sheriff of Nottingham receives a report from Sir Blackheart about progress by the Poison Ivy Legions. They have the task of clearing the forests where Robin Hood and his merry men live. The dastardly destroyers have already cleared William Tell out of his forest and now they are preparing new broadaxes for the forest around Robin Hood.
ACT 1 Scene 2 The Poison Ivy Legion appears in front of Curtains singing their theme song “Poison Ivy”. The Choir joins them.
ACT 2 Scene 1 Inside view of a Spacecraft, with a backdrop looking from space to a section of planet Earth below. The Curtains opens to reveal Buck Rogers and his crew orbiting and approaching mother Earth. They have come from the 21* century and realise through their viewers, that there’s trouble afoot in Sherwood forest, still in the 14" century. They decide to land in a clearing and help the two heroes in distress. ACT 3 Scene 1 In Sherwood Forest, around a campfire Robin Hood and merry men are discussing how they might repel the Legions of Sheriff Rogue. William Tell and family are also present, offering help to Robin and Little John. Suddenly they see a spacecraft arriving. ACT 3 Scene 2 Buck Rogers and crew introduce themselves, offering to use their future technology to right the wrongs.
ACT 4 Buck, Robin and William Tell capture the Poison Ivy Legion and apply the Thought Inducing helmets to them. Sheriff Rogue and Sir Blackheart suddenly arrive to inspect progress and too are captured by the 3 Heroes.
Buck and crew have to leave to catch the Time Warp.

THE PLAY
ACT 1
Curtains open to reveal a lavish “Sheriff's Chambers”. Sheriff is behind a huge desk in fancy robes, writing ona scroll with a long quill. There are guards in chain mail with spears, crossed swords over a mantel piece, scrolls on shelves. Attendants, court jesters, dancers if stage permits.
An attendant enters, Herald beckons, and attendant whispers in Herald’s ear. Attendant exits as Herald wiks towards Sheriff...
HERALD: (bowing, then in a loud voice) My Lord Sheriff, the knight of Forestry Works has arrived.
SHERIFF: (beckons) Then send him in. I’m waiting for his report on progress in
Sherwood Forest.
HERALD: (loudly to off-stage) Send in Sir Blackheart, Knight of Forestry
Works.
(Enter Sir Blackheart)
SHERIFF: Aah! Sir Blackheart. Let me have your report... (walks out from behind table)... how are things progressing in Sherwood?
BLACKHEART: Things are progressing very well my Lord. I have a legion of men in the forest. They have just finished clearing the whole area where that nuisance William Tell lives. We have cut down ALL the trees, got rid of ALL the animals... nothing could live there now. William Tell and his men have had to flee from the forest, my Lord.
